How do we know? $TSLA revolves around a product called JIRA, a bug database commonly used at software companies. At Tesla, JIRA tracks more than just software—it tracks *everything*. Weird A/C smell? JIRA ticket. Console glitch? JIRA ticket. Car catch on fire? JIRA ticket.

The auditors at PwC have been looking at something completely different, meanwhile: scanned paper of signatures from actual drop-offs of cars. The customer has to sign something, right? So that's what gets audited while $TSLA plays database games.

In about 2017, $TSLA introduced the "Delivery Count Type," a new way to store information about whether vehicles have been delivered. There are two options: New and Used. But since it's a manual setting, used cars can be "delivered" as "New."  Have they really done that? Oh yes. https://t.co/0d8CGF82Q6

4. Gap up/down  Should the tickers gap up/down past the designated triggers, wait for retest of the trigger. Ex: $AMD gaps down to 99.50 & within the first 15 mins it retests 99.95-100. Could be a good time to take a put position. Old supports often become resistance & vice versa

Suppose $AMD again breaks the 100 support and closes 11:00 5m candle at 99.90. The 100 support has become weaker. Take a position. The probability of a breakout/breakdown becomes higher the more times the level is broken.

2. Fakeouts/Stop losses  Taking losses is inevitable in trading. Our job is to minimize them. My rule here is -10% hard stop loss because you can always re-add the position.  Suppose you take a position from Ex a) $AMD immediately reverses and closes 10:50 5m candle at 110.15…

b) Risky: Playing the first sign of follow through. Ex: $AMD closes 5m candle at 10:45AM at 100.15 - No trigger. At 10:47AM, $AMD fails 100 support and closes 10:47 1m candle at 99.80. I would likely take a position off of key support failure.

There are two strategies I follow.  a) Conservative: Wait for a 5 minute candle to close through the trigger level. Ex: if an $AMD put trigger is under 100 and 5 minute candle closes at 10:45AM at 99.85, take the position.
